rows.label: Udp port
rows.help: UDP port the mod receives tracker data on (OpenTrack protocol).

rows.label: Second player udp port
rows.help: UDP port for player 2's tracker (OpenTrack protocol). Each player needs their own.

rows.label: Third player udp port
rows.help: UDP port for player 3's tracker (OpenTrack protocol). Each player needs their own.

rows.label: Fourth player udp port
rows.help: UDP port for player 4's tracker (OpenTrack protocol). Each player needs their own.

rows.label: Enable on startup
rows.help:
true: head tracking is on. Your tracker moves the first person view and turns your character's head in the isometric
view. false: it is off. No key turns it on or off. The options screen changes it when you apply, and an edit here
takes effect at the next start.

rows.label: World space yaw
rows.help:
true: turning your head left or right turns the view around the vertical, which keeps the horizon level while you look
up or down. false: it turns around the view's own up, which tilts the horizon while you look up or down. In a
vehicle seat it always turns around the view's own up.

rows.label: Rotation enabled
rows.help:
true: turning your head turns the view.
Tracking mode at startup, with PositionEnabled. The mode hotkey changes both.

rows.label: Data freshness ms
rows.help:
Milliseconds a tracker packet stays current. Once the tracker has sent nothing
for this long, the mod stops following it until data arrives again.

rows.label: First person enabled
rows.help:
true: the mod's first person view is there to switch to. false: saves load in the isometric view whatever FirstPerson
says, and with FirstPersonInVehicles on, first person comes on as you get into a vehicle. With both off there is no
first person view, the isometric view is the game's own whatever IsometricQuality says, and nothing more is made
ready for first person, though what is ready already stays until you leave the save. The first person key, or a
double tap of Back on a controller, then turns this on and switches to first person, and the graphics key turns it
on to go to an isometric graphics mode other than Low.
Takes effect at once. From the next start, off also stops the mod changing the game's own code for this.

rows.label: Third person enabled
rows.help:
true: the first person key goes on from first person to a third person view from behind your character, and from
there back to the isometric view. false: it switches between first person and the isometric view only.

rows.label: Field of view
rows.help: Vertical field of view of the first person view, in degrees: 40 to 110.

rows.label: Third person field of view
rows.help: Vertical field of view of the third person view, in degrees: 40 to 110.

rows.label: Mouse look speed
rows.help:
How fast the mouse turns the first and third person view: 1 is the mod's own speed, 0.5 half as fast, 2 twice as
fast, from 0.1 to 3.0. Your head's turns are your tracker's and do not change with it.

rows.label: Stick look speed
rows.help:
How fast a controller's aiming stick turns the first and third person view: 1 is the mod's own speed, 0.5 half as
fast, 2 twice as fast, from 0.1 to 3.0. Your head's turns are your tracker's and do not change with it.

rows.label: Quality
rows.help:
First person graphics mode: Low, Medium, High or Custom. Custom draws the [Graphics] rows. Every mode but Custom
draws at most 2560x1440 pixels, however large the window. Automatic, as the file comes, measures your PC once:
the first time first person shows, it starts at High, steps down while the picture is drawn fewer than 45 times
a second, and saves the mode that holds here. It never changes the mode after that.

rows.label: Isometric quality
rows.help:
Graphics mode of the game's isometric view: Low (the game's own picture), Medium, High or Custom, which draws the
[Graphics] rows.

rows.label: Style
rows.help:
Picture style: Vivid (strong contrast and colour), Natural (colours as lit, less contrast), Bleak (washed out, close
to the game's own look), Warm (golden light and amber shade) or Cold (steel blue shade and pale light). A new
style fades in over most of a second.

rows.label: First person
rows.help:
true: saves load in first person, while FirstPersonEnabled is on. Switching the view with the first person key, or a
double tap of Back on a controller, changes this to match.

rows.label: Third person
rows.help:
true: saves that load in first person load in the third person view instead, while ThirdPersonEnabled is on.
Switching the view changes this to match.

rows.label: First person in vehicles
rows.help:
true: getting into a vehicle switches to first person, and getting out switches back to the isometric view, even
with FirstPersonEnabled off. The first person key still switches the view at any time, and a view it chose is kept
when you get out.

rows.label: Hill height
rows.help:
How tall the first person hills are: 0 is as flat as the game's map, 1 is as the mod makes them, up to 2.0.
Always 1 where players can fight.

rows.label: Muzzle flash
rows.help: true: firing a gun flashes at the muzzle and briefly lights up what is nearby, in every graphics mode but Low.

rows.label: Crosshair
rows.help:
true: in first person, while the game draws no reticle of its own, a small crosshair with a weapon in hand, or a dot
without one, shows where the shot lands and what the interact key uses. false: neither is drawn.

rows.label: Regrip two handed weapons
rows.help:
true: a two-handed weapon goes back into both hands when your left hand puts down what it held beside it, as the
inventory's Equip Two Hands does. A light in your left hand is put away when you switch it off, so the weapon goes
back into both hands, and taking up a light leaves the weapon in your right hand. false: as in the game, the weapon
stays in your right hand alone, and taking up a light takes it out of your hands. Never on a server where players
can fight.

rows.label: Split screen
rows.help:
How two players share one screen: Vertical (side by side) or Horizontal (above and below). Takes effect at once.
Vertical is the game's own split screen, and from the next start the mod leaves that part of the game alone.

rows.label: Customise character head
rows.help:
true: on the game's Customise Character screen, the character shown turns its head as you turn yours, as your
reflection would, and if TalkingMouths was on as the game started, its mouth moves with what you say into your
microphone. false: it stands as the game poses it.
Takes effect at once. From the next start, off also stops the mod changing the game's own code for this.

rows.label: Local smoothing
rows.help: Smoothing for a tracker on this PC that sends to 127.0.0.1. 0 is the least, 1 the most.

rows.label: Remote smoothing
rows.help:
Smoothing for every other tracker: one on another device such as a phone, or one on this PC that sends to this PC's
network address instead of 127.0.0.1. 0 is the least, 1 the most.

rows.label: Position enabled
rows.help:
true: moving your head moves the view.
Tracking mode at startup, with RotationEnabled. The mode hotkey changes both.

rows.label: True free look
rows.help:
false: aiming down the sights keeps your eye on the sights when you lean. true: free look, the weapon stays put and your
head moves around it.

rows.label: Free look marker
rows.help: Changes nothing in Project Zomboid: the game's own reticle is the free look marker. Written with TrueFreeLook.

rows.label: Stock sights
rows.help:
true: while you aim down the sights your head stops moving the view, apart from tilting it,
so the sights sit in the centre as they do without head tracking. At the hip nothing changes.

rows.label: Position limit X
rows.help: How far, in metres, leaning left or right can move the view.

rows.label: Position limit Y
rows.help: How far, in metres, raising your head can move the view.

rows.label: Position limit Y down
rows.help: How far, in metres, lowering your head can move the view.

rows.label: Position limit Z
rows.help: How far, in metres, leaning forward can move the view.

rows.label: Position limit Z back
rows.help: How far, in metres, leaning back can move the view.

rows.label: Collision enabled
rows.help:
true: leaning your head stops at walls instead of moving the view through them. false: the lean is not held off
walls, so leaning into one can put the view through it.

rows.label: Collision margin
rows.help: How far the view is held off a wall when you lean into it, in map tiles.

rows.label: Collision release smoothing
rows.help:
How gently the view eases back out after a wall stopped a lean.
0 is the quickest, 1 the slowest.

rows.label: Cycle tracking mode key
rows.help: Changes the tracking mode: rotation and position, rotation only, position only.

rows.label: Yaw mode key
rows.help: Switches yaw between the world's up axis and the camera's own (WorldSpaceYaw).

rows.label: True free look key
rows.help: Cycles the aim mode: sights locked, free look with a marker, stock sights.

rows.label: First person key
rows.help:
Goes from the isometric view to first person, on to third person while ThirdPersonEnabled is on, and back to the
isometric view. Tap once for player 1, twice for player 2, three times for player 3, four times for player 4.
Held, it puts every player into first person if any is in the isometric view, or else every player back into it.
While Project Viewpoint, another mod, runs, Delete is left out, as Viewpoint opens its settings window on Delete.

rows.label: Cycle quality key
rows.help:
Goes to the next graphics mode of the view a player is in: in first person Low, Medium, High, Custom
(Quality), in the isometric view Low, Medium, High, Custom (IsometricQuality), and for players 2, 3 and 4 their
rows of [Players]. Tap once for player 1, twice for player 2, three times for player 3, four times for player 4,
or hold for every player. While Project Viewpoint, another mod, runs, F9 is left out, as Viewpoint takes a
screenshot on F9.

rows.label: Cycle style key
rows.help:
Goes to a player's next picture style: Vivid, Natural, Bleak, Warm, Cold (Style, and for players 2, 3 and 4
their rows of [Players]). Tap once for player 1, twice for player 2, three times for player 3, four times for
player 4, or hold for every player.

rows.label: Split screen key
rows.help: With two players at the screen, switches between side by side and above and below.

rows.label: Light multiplier
rows.help:
How far the flashlight turns for each degree your head turns, while TorchFollowsHead is on. 1 turns it as far as
the view, more turns it further, and 0 leaves it where your character faces.

rows.label: Torch follows head
rows.help:
true: in first person, a flashlight you carry points where your head turns, as far as LightMultiplier says.
false: it points the way your character faces, whatever your head does.

rows.label: Hear from the eye
rows.help:
true: in first person you hear from your character's eyes: sounds turn with the view, walls between you and a sound
muffle it, and rooms echo. false: you hear as the isometric view does, facing north-west on the map.
Takes effect when the game next starts. When off, the mod does not change the game's own code for this.

rows.label: Lightning bolts
rows.help:
true: in first person, lightning strikes as a bolt from the clouds to the ground and lights up the world while it
flashes. false: the game's own lightning, a flash that brightens the whole map for a moment.
Takes effect when the game next starts. When off, the mod does not change the game's own code for this.

rows.label: Shot impacts
rows.help:
true: in first person, in Medium and High, a shot kicks up dust, chips, splinters, sparks or blood where it hits
and leaves a hole, and in autumn knocks leaves loose from the trees and bushes it passes through. false: shots
leave no mark and knock no leaves loose, as in the game's own view. Shots still break lamps and glass
and hole doors, walls and fences when ShotsBreakLamps, ShotsBreakGlass, BlastHoles and BulletHoles are on, and
while any of them is on, the mod keeps changing the game's code for this.
Takes effect at once. From the next start, off also stops the mod changing the game's own code for this.

rows.label: Falling debris
rows.help:
true: in first person, a fence, lamp post or road barricade a vehicle knocks down throws pieces of itself, and
what shots cut out of a fence, a wall or a door drops out of it: the pieces bounce, lie a few seconds and sink into the
ground. They are only in the picture and nothing touches them. false: no pieces: what is knocked down or shot
out goes from the picture at once.

rows.label: Lamp shadows
rows.help:
true: in first person, in Medium and High, the street lamps, lamps and ceiling lights nearest you that are on at
night cast shadows of what stands in their light: fences, furniture, people and zombies. High has more of them
cast shadows, and sharper. false: what stands under a lamp casts no shadow from it.

rows.label: Coloured glass light
rows.help:
true: in first person, in Medium and High, sunlight through a stained glass window takes the colours of its
glass onto whatever it falls on behind it, and into the air of the room. false: a stained glass window lets no
sunlight through in those modes.

rows.label: Far vehicles and zombies
rows.help:
true: in first person, vehicles, zombies and animals in sight are drawn even past the edge of the game's own
screen, and so are other players where players cannot fight. false: each is drawn only where the game's own
view would show it.

rows.label: Far land detail
rows.help:
true: in first person, the land past the edge of the loaded map takes its colours from what the map lays there:
each square the colour of its floor, road, pavement, grass or sand, and each building its own walls' and roof's
colours, its windows where the map has windows, and its roof pitched where the map's roof slopes. false: the land
there is the colours of the game's map, and its buildings are blocks in a few plain colours with flat roofs.

rows.label: Modded vehicle interiors
rows.help:
true: in first person, from the seat of a vehicle a mod adds, the dashboard, steering wheel and seats the mod puts
in it are drawn, the windows it adds as parts of their own are left out so you see out through them, and the
driver's eye is put behind the steering wheel the mod models. Such a cabin keeps its own colours: the mod does
not repaint its seats and dashboard or darken its footwell, as it does for the game's own cars. Road wheels are
left out by the vehicle's own list of them. false: any part whose model or shader is named for a wheel is left
out from the seat, which leaves some vehicle mods with no dashboard, their windows are drawn as solid, and the
driver's eye is put from the game's seat.

rows.label: Quick ragdolls
rows.help:
true: while anyone plays in first person, a body that is hit switches to its ragdoll at once, and a first person
shot pushes it along the shot from where it went in. false: bodies switch to their ragdolls the way the
game blends them in.
Takes effect when the game next starts. When off, the mod does not change the game's own code for this.

rows.label: Hit flinch
rows.help:
true: a zombie shot in first person that stays on its feet reacts where the bullet hit: its head snaps back or
its shoulder spins round. false: it plays only the game's own stagger.

rows.label: Hit direction
rows.help:
true: in first person, a red arc at the edge of the view points to whoever hits you or a zombie that goes for you, and
follows them as you turn while it fades, and a zombie within two tiles out of your view, that the game would show
you in its own view, puts a faint red glow on the edge it is on. Where players can hurt each other, a player who
hits you is pointed to only while the game shows you that player. false: neither.

rows.label: Head led view when down
rows.help:
true: in first person, when you are knocked over, lie down, get up or die, the view follows your character's
head. false: the mouse keeps the view while the game moves the body, and when you die the view stays where it was.

rows.label: Items as models
rows.help:
true: in first person, items on the ground are shown as the game's own 3D models of them, while the game's 3D
ground items option is on. false: each lies flat as its picture.
Takes effect at once. From the next start, off also stops the mod changing the game's own code for this.

rows.label: Finer skins
rows.help:
true: in first person, people near you wear more detailed skins than the game's: the mod's own, and any finer
ones in the folder the log names. false: they wear the game's own.
Takes effect when the game next starts. When off, the mod does not change the game's own code for this.

rows.label: Leave out screen grey
rows.help:
true: the game's grey tint for the season, fog and weather is left off the first person picture, which shows those
with its own lighting. false: the game tints the first person picture as it tints its own view.
Takes effect when the game next starts. When off, the mod does not change the game's own code for this.

rows.label: Wet on the player
rows.help:
true: in first person, in Medium and High, rain wets your hands, your sleeves and what you hold over about a minute:
cloth and skin darken, metal and wood shine, and drops bead on them and run down the weapon. Snow that melts
on you indoors wets them too. Out of the rain, indoors, under a roof or in a vehicle they dry over a few minutes,
and clothes the game has soaked stay dark until the game dries them. false: they stay dry whatever the weather.

rows.label: Aim blur
rows.help:
true: in first person, in Medium and High, with a gun's sights up the background beyond what you aim at softens a
little, and the nearest parts of the gun a little less, eased in and out as the sights come up and go down. A
target close by softens the background more than one far off. Never through a scope. false: the picture stays
sharp from the gun to the horizon.

rows.label: Gran turismo tone mapping
rows.help:
true: in first person, in every graphics mode but Low, light is brought into the screen's range as Gran Turismo 7
does it, with Polyphony Digital's tone mapping: deeper shadows, brighter middle tones, and bright light reaching
white sooner. false: the mod's own film curve, softer at both ends.

rows.label: Name tags at heads
rows.help:
true: on a server, in first person, the names and speech the game shows over people sit over their heads in the
picture, and your own are hidden. false: the game shows them where its own view puts them.
Takes effect when the game next starts. When off, the mod does not change the game's own code for this.

rows.label: Captions over sets
rows.help:
true: in first person, the lines a television, a radio or a car radio shows of what it is playing sit over the
set in the picture, and those of a radio you carry or of the car you sit in low in the middle, over the panels
along the bottom. false: the game shows a set's where its own view puts them, and a radio you carry's with
your own speech, which NameTagsAtHeads hides.
Takes effect when the game next starts. When off, the mod does not change the game's own code for this.

rows.label: Highlights
rows.help:
true: in first person, a line is drawn round what the Interact key would act on, and round what the game highlights
or marks on the ground for you, such as the container the loot panel shows. false: none of them, for immersion.
The piece of furniture you are placing is still outlined.

rows.label: Interact label
rows.help:
true: in first person, a short line under the crosshair says what the Interact key would do to what it is on, such
as Open Door or Grab and the item's name, and what holding the key does where that is different. false: no line.

rows.label: Inventory stays open
rows.help:
true: in first person, your inventory and the loot panel stay open on the screen while you look around. The loot
panel shows the container, body or items on the ground the crosshair is on within reach, or with the crosshair
on none of those, a body you stand over. The inventory key or a middle click brings the mouse pointer out to use
them, and the same again or Escape goes back to looking, with them open again. They fold while you aim.
false: they open with the inventory key or Interact on a container, and close again as you go back to looking.

rows.label: Quick loot
rows.help:
true: in first person, with the crosshair on a container or a body within reach, a short list of what is in it
stands beside the crosshair, with the container's weight against what it holds. A tap of the Interact key takes
the highlighted item, holding it takes everything, and the mouse wheel, or up and down on a controller's d-pad,
moves the highlight. The inventory key opens the game's panels with the container in the loot panel.
false: no list, and a tap of the Interact key on a container shows it in the loot panel.
Takes effect at once. From the next start, off also stops the mod changing the game's own code for this.

rows.label: Figures behind walls
rows.help:
true: in first person, a zombie, person or animal against a wall, a shut door or a fence you cannot see through is
not drawn reaching, leaning or poking through it to your side. false: they are drawn as the game poses them, so a
hand, a shoulder or a head can show through.

rows.label: Overarm throw
rows.help:
true: in first person, a Molotov, a pipe bomb or anything else you throw is drawn back over your shoulder and thrown
overarm. false: it is swung as a one-handed weapon is.

rows.label: Fishing rod
rows.help:
true: in first person, a fishing rod out over water is held with your left hand on its reel, swung back and out to
cast, lifted while you reel in, and its line runs from its tip to the bobber. false: the rod is held as a swung
weapon is, and no line is drawn. The bobber is drawn where it floats either way.

rows.label: Surroundings in reflections
rows.help:
true: in first person, in High, wet roads, puddles, polished floors and window glass also mirror the buildings,
ground and trees round you that are off the edge of the screen or behind something nearer, from a small picture of
your surroundings kept up as you move. People and vehicles are not in it. In Custom it needs ShadingAndLight and
Reflections on and ReflectionScale at 0.75 or more. false: they mirror only what is on the screen, and the sky where
that runs out.

rows.label: Watch glance
rows.help:
true: in first person, with a watch on a wrist and that hand free, looking down and then to that side raises the arm
and turns the wrist so you can read the watch, standing or walking: the time as the game's clock shows it, in figures
on a digital watch and as hands on any other. While head tracking is on only your head's look counts, and the mouse
never raises it; with it off, the mouse's look does. With a watch on each wrist, the one you turn to. Not while
aiming or attacking. false: the arm stays down.

rows.label: Held map
rows.help:
true: in first person, a tap of the map key puts the game's map in both hands at once, standing, walking or running,
the place round you on it, and it stays up until you put it down. In a vehicle seat it is held low in the right hand,
and a driver keeps the left on the wheel. Another tap puts it down. Holding the map key, or the map button on the side
bar, opens the game's map over the screen, to pan, zoom and mark. Esc or a middle click puts it down and does nothing
else. Where the game says it is too dark to read the map, it does not come up. Opening or shutting a door leaves it up.
Aiming, attacking, starting anything else, getting into or out of a seat, or leaving first person puts it down.
On a server where players can fight, the game's map opens as it does without the mod. false: the map key opens the
game's map over the screen, as without the mod.
Takes effect at once. From the next start, off also stops the mod changing the game's own code for this.

rows.label: Second player quality
rows.help: Player 2's first person graphics mode, as Quality.

rows.label: Second player isometric quality
rows.help: Player 2's isometric graphics mode, as IsometricQuality.

rows.label: Second player style
rows.help: Player 2's picture style, as Style.

rows.label: Second player first person
rows.help: Player 2's view at load, as FirstPerson.

rows.label: Second player third person
rows.help: Player 2's third person at load, as ThirdPerson.

rows.label: Second player first person in vehicles
rows.help: Player 2's view in vehicles, as FirstPersonInVehicles.

rows.label: Third player quality
rows.help: Player 3's first person graphics mode, as Quality.

rows.label: Third player isometric quality
rows.help: Player 3's isometric graphics mode, as IsometricQuality.

rows.label: Third player style
rows.help: Player 3's picture style, as Style.

rows.label: Third player first person
rows.help: Player 3's view at load, as FirstPerson.

rows.label: Third player third person
rows.help: Player 3's third person at load, as ThirdPerson.

rows.label: Third player first person in vehicles
rows.help: Player 3's view in vehicles, as FirstPersonInVehicles.

rows.label: Fourth player quality
rows.help: Player 4's first person graphics mode, as Quality.

rows.label: Fourth player isometric quality
rows.help: Player 4's isometric graphics mode, as IsometricQuality.

rows.label: Fourth player style
rows.help: Player 4's picture style, as Style.

rows.label: Fourth player first person
rows.help: Player 4's view at load, as FirstPerson.

rows.label: Fourth player third person
rows.help: Player 4's third person at load, as ThirdPerson.

rows.label: Fourth player first person in vehicles
rows.help: Player 4's view in vehicles, as FirstPersonInVehicles.

rows.label: Tree quality
rows.help:
Low: the game's plant sprites. Medium: the mod's trees, with the game's sprites past 40 tiles.
High: the mod's trees as far as you can see.

rows.label: Grass density
rows.help:
How much of the grass the mod grows blade by blade is grown, as a percentage: 10 to 100.
Lower, fewer and broader plants cover the same lawns and long grass, which costs less to build and draw. High
grows all of it and Medium 40. On a server where players can hurt each other it grows all of it.
With TreeQuality Low the mod grows no grass of its own.

rows.label: Grass distance
rows.help:
How far from you lawns are grown blade by blade in first person, in tiles: 8 to 48. Past that, lawns are flat. Higher
costs more to build and draw. Medium and High grow lawns to 16 tiles. Long grass is not affected.
With TreeQuality Low the mod grows no grass of its own.

rows.label: Render scale
rows.help: How much of the window's resolution the first person picture is drawn at, each way: 0.5 to 1.

rows.label: View distance
rows.help: How far the first person view is drawn, in tiles: 32 to 80, within the map the game has loaded.

rows.label: Zombies and props draw distance
rows.help:
How far zombies, people, vehicles and the mod's furniture are drawn, in tiles: 16 to 80, never past
ViewDistance. Where players can fight, everything is drawn.

rows.label: Far tree distance
rows.help: How far past the loaded map trees are drawn, in tiles: 0 (none) to 768.

rows.label: Rain on glass
rows.help:
Rain on your vehicle's windows: Low (one size of drop), Medium (adds specks and trickles) or High (three sizes and
running drops).

rows.label: Shading and light
rows.help:
true: shaded corners, light from things nearby and lit air, and with Reflections, wet roads, floors, glass and water
that mirror the world.

rows.label: Reflections
rows.help:
true: mirrors in rooms show the room and you, your vehicle's mirrors show the road behind, and with
ShadingAndLight, wet roads, floors, glass and water mirror the world.

rows.label: Reflection scale
rows.help:
How much of the first person picture's resolution wall mirrors and window glass draw their reflections at, each
way: 0.25 to 1. High draws 0.75, Medium 0.5. Lower costs less and looks softer.

rows.label: Full size textures
rows.help: true: the mod's surface, wall and skin pictures at full size. false: half size, using a quarter of the memory.

rows.label: Surface depth
rows.help: true: near surfaces get the depth of what they show. false: they are drawn flat.

rows.label: Sharp shadows
rows.help: true: shadow maps 4096 pixels across. false: 2048, using a quarter of the graphics memory.

rows.label: Whole figure shadows
rows.help:
true: what people and zombies wear and carry casts a shadow at any distance. false: past 4 tiles only
their bodies do, which costs less in a crowd.

rows.label: Frame blending
rows.help:
true: each frame is blended with the ones before it (temporal anti-aliasing), which smooths grass, leaves and fine
edges that Antialiasing alone cannot, for a slightly softer picture. Medium and High use it.

rows.label: Antialiasing
rows.help:
How jagged edges are smoothed, from each frame alone: Off; Low, a quick blend across each edge; Medium, which also
follows each edge to its ends so long shallow edges come out even; High, which follows them further and catches
fainter ones too. The Low, Medium and High graphics modes use Low, whose slight softening also calms the shimmer
of FrameBlending; Medium and High only touch the edges, for a sharper picture.

rows.label: Upscaling
rows.help:
How the picture is brought up to the screen's size when it is drawn at fewer pixels than the screen: Bilinear, each
pixel read between the four nearest, with a fixed sharpening; FSR, AMD's FSR 1 Super Resolution, which follows
edges as it enlarges and then sharpens by how much contrast is round each pixel. A picture drawn at the screen's
size is shown the same either way. The Low, Medium and High graphics modes use FSR, in first person and isometric.

rows.label: Light distance
rows.help:
How far away lamps light what is around them with light of their own, like the pool of light under a street lamp,
in tiles: 0 (the game's light only) to 80. Past that, lamps light the ground as the game does.

rows.label: Corpse models
rows.help:
true: corpses are drawn as models lying where they fell, as zombies are. false: as the game's flat picture of each,
laid on the ground, which costs far less where many lie. The Low, Medium and High graphics modes use the models.

rows.label: Spread light updates
rows.help:
true: when the game relights many places at once, the first person view takes in their new light over the next few
frames, nearest first, so driving past lights stutters less. false: all of it in the frame the game relights it,
so a far light change can show about a tenth of a second sooner, in longer frames.

rows.label: Cached game lookups
rows.help:
true: the game's lookups of items by name, of component classes and of character state machines are answered from
what they found before, and two of its bone updates skip work that changes nothing, in both views. The
results are the same. false: the game works each one out every time.
Takes effect when the game next starts. When off, the mod does not change the game's own code for this.

rows.label: Skip covered game drawing
rows.help:
true: while the first person picture covers the screen, the game skips drawing its own view underneath it: its
weather, floors, objects, shadows, people and the rest. What you see is the same. false: the game draws its
whole view under the picture every frame.
Takes effect at once. From the next start, off also stops the mod changing the game's own code for this.

rows.label: Skins composed while waiting
rows.help:
true: while the first person picture covers the game's view, what characters wear is built into their skins while
the render thread waits for the next frame. The skins look the same. false: the game builds them in the
middle of drawing the frame.
Takes effect at once. From the next start, off also stops the mod changing the game's own code for this.

rows.label: Chunk change counts
rows.help:
true: the game's changes to each chunk are counted as it makes them, so the first person view rebuilds only the
chunks that changed. What you see is the same. false: the view checks every chunk it draws for changes.
Takes effect when the game next starts. When off, the mod does not change the game's own code for this.

rows.label: Unseen room zombies unmodelled
rows.help:
true: in first person, a zombie in a room you could not see into, even with every nearby door and curtain open,
has no model until you come close enough to see in. false: it keeps its model wherever it stands.

rows.label: Hold chunk map centre
rows.help:
true: the game's map of loaded chunks keeps its centre until you are a tile past a chunk edge, so turning on the
spot right on an edge does not load a column of chunks again every few seconds. false: as in the game, the
centre moves to your chunk at once.
Takes effect at once. From the next start, off also stops the mod changing the game's own code for this.

rows.label: Graphics memory steps
rows.help:
true: on an NVIDIA graphics card without enough memory for what a graphics mode draws, first person starts the
session drawing less in every mode. false: every mode starts as it is. Checked when first person first
starts in a session. Either way, when the card runs out of room for something the mod makes, every mode
drops a step.

rows.label: Prepare while loading
rows.help:
true: a save starts only once the mod's shaders are compiled and the distant land and the skins around you are
made, so first person does not stutter making them during play. false: the save starts as soon as the game
is ready, and first person makes them as you play.
Takes effect at once. From the next start, off also stops the mod changing the game's own code for this.

rows.label: Spot by sight
rows.help:
true: under the first person picture, the rooms the game fills with zombies and the squares it counts as seen
follow what the view sees, a few times a second. false: they follow where the mod has the game work out
light, which can fill a room you have not looked into. Needs SkipCoveredGameDrawing.
Takes effect at once. From the next start, off also stops the mod changing the game's own code for this.

rows.label: Build on worker threads
rows.help:
true: the first person view rebuilds chunks on threads of its own, all at once, and shows each one a frame
later. false: each is rebuilt on the game's own thread as the view reaches it, and shows in that frame.

rows.label: Rebuild for own sprites
rows.help:
true: a chunk the first person view built before some of its sprites or pictures had loaded is rebuilt once
those have. false: it is rebuilt whenever any sprite or picture loads, which for the first seconds after
arriving somewhere is most frames.

rows.label: Hidden wall reads kept
rows.help:
true: as chunks load, what HiddenWallDecor reads from a building for each room it decorates is kept, and only
the chunks the game has changed since are read again. The rooms come out the same. Needs ChunkChangeCounts.
false: the whole building is read again for each chunk that loads, which can hitch in a tall building.

rows.label: Building facts kept
rows.help:
true: what a building's room names say, what kind of place each room is, whether the building is a home and what
each picture shows are worked out once and kept. The rooms and their pictures come out the same.
false: they are worked out again for each room, which can hitch in a tall building.

rows.label: Vanilla weapons
rows.help:
true: the game's own weapons, with no picture through the scope. false: the mod's models of the pump shotgun and
its sawn-off, the tactical pump shotgun, the hunting, varmint and tactical rifles, the lever action rifle and
carbine, the self-loading rifle and carbine, the double barrelled shotgun and its sawn-off, the pistols, the
revolvers, the toy cap pistol and rifle, the assault rifle, the battle rifle and rifle scopes.

rows.label: Vanilla furniture
rows.help:
true: the game's sprites. false: the mod's models of furniture, appliances, street lamps, clocks, picture frames,
banners and flags.

rows.label: Vanilla pictures
rows.help:
true: the game's pictures on walls, and only colour bars on a television. false: the mod's own pictures on walls
and televisions, where it has one.

rows.label: Vanilla plants
rows.help:
true: the game's sprites. false: the mod's trees, bushes, boulders, grass, ferns, flowers, crops, fallen leaves and
fallen sticks.

rows.label: Vanilla textures
rows.help:
true: the colours of the game's sprites, and its own stained glass. false: the mod's textures of ground, wood,
roofing, paint, carpet, cloth, wallpaper and stained glass, and clean road lines.

rows.label: Vanilla buildings
rows.help:
true: the game's sprites. false: windows, doors, curtains, handrails, chain link fences, open stairs, railway
track and wall finishes built by the mod.

rows.label: Vanilla zombies
rows.help: true: the game's own skins for zombies. false: the mod's skins, with lifelike faces, for zombies near you.

rows.label: Vanilla people
rows.help:
true: the game's own skins for people. false: the mod's skins, with lifelike faces, for your character and other
living people.

rows.label: Vanilla arms
rows.help:
true: the game's own arms and hands on a held weapon, for a mod that changes the arms or the weapons. false: the
mod's arms and hands, which work the bolt, slide and magazine.

rows.label: Vanilla clothes
rows.help:
true: the game's own pictures of clothes and hair. false: clothes and hair near you are sharpened, with the weave,
knit, grain or strands of what they are made of.

rows.label: Vanilla animals
rows.help: true: the game's own skins for animals. false: the mod's skins for animals near you, with the hair of their coats.

rows.label: Vanilla fire
rows.help:
true: the game's own flames and smoke, standing upright where they burn. false: the game's flames with the mod's
smoke, embers and firelight for burning buildings, Molotovs, campfires, fireplaces, wood stoves, burn barrels
and cooking pits.

rows.label: Vanilla cabins
rows.help:
true: the game's own inside of the vehicle you sit in, with its glass cut away. false: the mod's model of the inside,
with its dashboard, instruments, wheel, seats and doors.

rows.label: Furniture decor
rows.help:
true: with the mod's furniture, what the game paints over a piece of it is made as part of the model where the mod
has a model of it: a kitchen counter's door the game paints standing ajar stands open on its hinges. false: what
the game paints over the furniture stands on it as the game's picture.

rows.label: Shots through walls
rows.help:
true: your shots go on through stud walls, plank walls, shut doors and windows, losing damage to each by what it
is made of. false: they stop at them, as in the game. On a server where players can hurt each other the game's
rule applies.
Takes effect at once. With this and FirstPersonEnabled both off, the mod stops changing the game's own code for
this from the next start.

rows.label: Shots break lamps
rows.help:
true: offline, a shot breaks a lamp it passes through and a vehicle light it hits. false: lamps stay lit, as in the
game. On a server the game's rule applies.

rows.label: Shots break glass
rows.help:
true: offline, a shot breaks the glass of every shut window it crosses, whether or not it hits anything behind it.
false: only a shot that hits someone through a window breaks it, as in the game. On a server the game's rule
applies.

rows.label: Shots wound limbs
rows.help:
true: offline, first person shots to a zombie's legs slow it and drop it to a crawl, shots to its arms leave them
hanging, enough take the limb off, and a killing head shot can take the head off or burst it. false: hits are
the game's. On a server the game's rule applies.

rows.label: Vehicles smash through
rows.help:
true: offline, a vehicle going faster than walking pace knocks down fences, street lamp posts and road barricades,
drives through bushes without slowing and keeps its engine's full power off the road. false: the game's rules
for all of it. On a server the game's rules apply.
Takes effect at once. From the next start, off also stops the mod changing the game's own code for this.

rows.label: Faces the view
rows.help:
true: moving sideways or backwards in first person, your character keeps facing where you look and goes at up
to a jog, and sprints only ahead or on a forward diagonal. false: it always turns, as in the game. On a
server where players can hurt each other it keeps facing where you look when going sideways and backwards, on
or off, at the slower pace the game gives its aiming stance.

rows.label: Shots past trees
rows.help:
true: a tree stops your shots only where its trunk is drawn, and a shot past the trunk goes on. false: a tree stops
every shot across its square, as in the game. On a server where players can hurt each other the game's rule
applies.

rows.label: Zombies seen at once
rows.help:
true: in the isometric view a zombie shows as soon as nothing stands between your character and it, within the
reach of your character's sight by the game's rules. false: the game's own sight, which can show a zombie late
or only once it is close. On a server where players can hurt each other the game's rule applies.
Takes effect at once. From the next start, off also stops the mod changing the game's own code for this.

rows.label: Hidden wall decor
rows.help:
true: in first person, the south and east walls of a room, which the isometric view never shows from inside, get
pictures drawn by the mod and never saved. false: nothing is drawn on them, and nothing is added to them
whatever HiddenWallDecorSaved says. On a server the pictures are drawn too.
Takes effect at once. With this and FirstPersonEnabled both off, the mod stops changing the game's own code for
this from the next start.

rows.label: Hidden wall decor saved
rows.help:
true: offline, while HiddenWallDecor is on, those walls also get the game's own mirrors, clocks and coat racks where
the room's other walls say they belong, the first time the room is loaded, and those stay in your save.
false: nothing is added to the save, and what was added before stays. On a server nothing is added.

rows.label: Blast holes
rows.help:
true: offline, a shotgun blast in first person whose pellets land close together on a wooden door, a wooden
fence or a wall of boards or plasterboard blows a ragged hole through it that you can see and shoot through,
the pellets that miss the hole leave marks on a door, and each pellet that strikes a picket of a picket fence
breaks it. The holes and the broken pickets stay in your save. false: shots leave doors, fences and walls
whole. On a server they stay whole.

rows.label: Bullet holes
rows.help:
true: offline, while ShotsThroughWalls is on, a round you fire in first person that goes through a door, a wall
or a fence leaves a small hole where it went in and a wider, splintered one where it came out, which you can
see through, and one that strikes a picket of a picket fence breaks it: struck between its rails it falls out
whole, above or below them it breaks off there. The holes and the broken pickets stay in your save. false:
rounds still go through, and leave only a mark. On a server nothing is holed or broken.

rows.label: Climb through holes
rows.help:
true: offline, in first person, holding the Interact key with the crosshair on a hole shot through a fence,
a wall or a door, where the hole is wide and tall enough for you to fit through and you stand beside it,
climbs you through. false: holes are only to see and shoot through. On a server nothing is climbed through.

rows.label: Vehicles stay upright in turns
rows.help:
true: offline, a vehicle turned hard, or slid round with the brakes on, leans less than the game's physics
leans it. false: it leans as the game's physics has it. On a server the game's physics applies.
Takes effect at once. With this and HillsMoveVehicles both off, the mod stops changing the game's own code for
this from the next start.

rows.label: Shots from vehicle seats
rows.help:
true: in first person, sitting in a vehicle with a gun, you can fire through any part of your seat's window, and
the shot breaks it. false: as in the game, the window has to be opened or broken first. On a server where
players can hurt each other, the game's rule applies.

rows.label: Drive while aiming
rows.help:
true: in first person, driving with the keyboard, you can still steer, accelerate and brake while aiming a gun.
false: as in the game, aiming a gun takes over the controls. With a controller, and on a server where
players can hurt each other, the game's rule applies.

rows.label: Hills move vehicles
rows.help:
true: offline, driving in first person, hills pull a vehicle down them and can throw it into the air over a crest
at speed. false: vehicles move as on the game's level ground. On a server they always do.
Takes effect at once. With this and VehiclesStayUprightInTurns both off, the mod stops changing the game's own code
for this from the next start.

rows.label: Hand light out at the wheel
rows.help:
true: in first person, a light in your hands is switched off when you take the driver's seat, since your hands
are on the wheel. false: it stays as it was.

rows.label: Burnt building freeze fix
rows.help:
true: stops the game freezing for good while it sets up a burnt-down building whose door or window reaches into a
chunk that has not loaded yet. false: the game's own code, which can loop on that door forever.
Takes effect when the game next starts. When off, the mod does not change the game's own code for this.

rows.label: Centre the window
rows.help:
true: the game's window is centred in the part of the monitor the taskbar leaves free. false: the game centres it
on the whole main monitor, which can leave part of it under the taskbar.
Takes effect when the game next starts. When off, the mod does not change the game's own code for this.

rows.label: Controller choice fix
rows.help:
true: the controllers you tick in the game's options stay ticked, a 3Dconnexion 6-axis mouse is never used as a
controller, and the main menu goes to the controller whose A button was pressed. false: the game picks its
controllers, which with none ticked is the first one, a SpaceMouse if one was plugged in first.
Takes effect when the game next starts. When off, the mod does not change the game's own code for this.

rows.label: Talking mouths
rows.help:
true: your character's mouth moves with what you say into your microphone: the jaw drops for "ah", the lips spread
for "ee" and round for "oo". Online, other players' mouths move while the game's voice chat plays them, and
other players with this mod see your mouth move. The sound is never recorded or sent. false: no microphone is
opened. Takes effect at once, but at the next start for the people the game draws itself, as in the isometric view
at Low. With this and FirstPersonEnabled both off, the mod stops changing the game's own code for this from the
next start.

rows.label: Microphone
rows.help: Your microphone, by the name the system gives it, Default for the system's own default, or None.

rows.label: Second player microphone
rows.help: The microphone of player 2 at the screen, by the name the system gives it, Default for the system's own default, or None.

rows.label: Third player microphone
rows.help: The microphone of player 3 at the screen, by the name the system gives it, Default for the system's own default, or None.

rows.label: Fourth player microphone
rows.help: The microphone of player 4 at the screen, by the name the system gives it, Default for the system's own default, or None.
